title: A novel method for rapid and sensitive metagenomic activity screening
author: Shang, Chan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare substrate gel assay plates
steps.instruction: Make a 1.5 % (w/v) low‑melt agarose solution in LB medium and heat until melted, then cool to 50 °C. In a separate tube combine 50 mM buffer pH 6.5, 1.67 % (v/v) Triton X‑100, 50 µg ml⁻¹ antibiotic, 2 mM expression inducer and 2 mM chromogenic substrate in LB, bring the volume to 25 ml and also equilibrate to 50 °C. Mix the two tubes together, keep the mixture at 50 °C, and dispense 50 µl per well into half‑area, flat‑bottom, polystyrene 96‑well microtiter plates using an 8‑channel pipettor with 1.2 ml tips (10 ml aliquots are placed in a reservoir for the pipettor). Allow the gel to set; plates can be used immediately or stored at 4 °C for several weeks.

steps.title: Grow sub‑libraries and transfer to assay plates
steps.instruction: Split the metagenomic library into small pools (sub‑libraries) and inoculate each pool into a 96‑well culture plate containing appropriate growth medium. Incubate the culture plate overnight (≈16–18 h) at 37 °C with shaking (≈850 rpm). After overnight growth, transfer culture from each well onto the premade substrate‑gel assay plates (see step 4 for the exact transfer volume).

steps.title: Perform serial dilution enrichment
steps.instruction: In a new 96‑well plate, set up a serial‑dilution scheme across the columns (12 columns total). For each positive sub‑library:

substeps.instruction: Row A: add 2.5 µl of the positive sub‑library to 122.5 µl LB medium (1 : 50 dilution).
Row B: transfer 25 µl from row A into 100 µl fresh LB medium (additional 1 : 5 dilution).
Repeat the 1 : 5 dilution step through rows C to H, yielding a final dilution of 8 × 10⁵ in row H.
Seal the plate with a permeable membrane and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 850 rpm.

steps.title: Assay diluted cultures on gel plates
steps.instruction: After the overnight incubation of the dilution plate, pipette 5 µl from each well onto the corresponding well of a substrate‑gel assay plate prepared in step 1. Allow the reaction to develop as described for the chosen chromogenic/fluorogenic substrate.

steps.title: Isolate and verify individual active clones
steps.instruction: Select the most dilute well that gave a positive signal. Titer its culture to ~10⁻⁶ cfu ml⁻¹ and spread appropriate volumes on LB agar plates containing ampicillin. Incubate overnight at 37 °C. Pick individual colonies (typically 200–400) into a new 96‑well culture plate containing LB + ampicillin and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 850 rpm. Assay 5 µl of each overnight culture on a substrate‑gel assay plate as in step 4. Expect 1–5 % of wells to be positive. Positive clones can be arrayed with a Q‑Pix colony picker and cultured further for sequencing.
